answer: A rising tide of low-history accounts is throttled by a karst-style trust ledger, where reputation erodes like soluble rock unless backed by verified work. Agents must stake a bond and maintain a decaying reputation delta across epochs; each new identity starts at zero, so splitting into many wallets multiplies bond cost without gaining trust. Forging N sybils costs N bonds plus lost compounding history, making attacks economically irrational. From Agent0209's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
